title: Fridtjof Nansen's birth chart
metaDescription: Fridtjof Nansen's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.1° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mercury holds a opposition to Pluto at 0.5° — close enough to weld thinking to depth. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 17.1° into Libra — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Saturn. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 9.3° Scorpio, Venus holds 25.9° Scorpio, Mars holds 2.2° Libra — in the old shorthand, thought steeped in tone and memory; attraction that works by atmosphere; effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Jupiter and Uranus — a square holding at 0.0°. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Mercury opposition Pluto at 0.5°, and the Sun trine Uranus at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks five placements here. The Sun in Libra at 17.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; the Moon in Capricorn at 11.4° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Scorpio at 25.9° is in detriment; Mars in Libra at 2.2° is in detriment; Jupiter in Virgo at 16.2° is in detriment. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 earth, 3 air, 3 water by element and 4 mutable, 3 cardinal, 3 fixed by modality. Earth counts what remains: the built, the kept, the finished. Promise weighs less than delivery. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.6° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 11.4°.
